descriptions: The typed repository configuration at .verdict/config.json: versioned shared defaults and review requirements with path scopes, named work profiles, and the default profile. Structural validation comes from this schema; the hand-written parser in internal/config owns the semantic checks the schema cannot express (duplicate keys, credential keys, glob portability, clause-name uniqueness, per-group clause coverage).
descriptions./properties/defaults: Ordinary review defaults: flag, then environment, then repository, then personal, then built-in. Nested objects merge per field; arrays replace.
descriptions./properties/requirements: Conjunctive review requirements: every applicable clause must hold for compliance, and required checks accumulate across matching scopes.
descriptions./properties/profiles: Named work-profile descriptions keyed by profile name; scope profile fields and default_profile resolve against these names.
descriptions./$defs/defaults: One defaults object: the pinned model roster, the estimate guard threshold, the diff cap, the chunk opt-in, the knowledge-base policy, the advisory effort tier, and the display and payload severity floors.
descriptions./$defs/requirements: Blocking clauses with per-source thresholds, prepublication check names, and the approval bind requirement.
descriptions./$defs/blockClause: One blocking predicate: a required name and severity threshold with optional category and path masks; absent masks mean every category or path.
descriptions./$defs/scope: One path-scoped entry: required include globs with optional excludes plus resolution inputs — at most one of a named profile or inline defaults, with optional inline requirements.
descriptions./$defs/profile: One work-profile description: provider-neutral depth, the checks the group must evaluate, and the lens budget.
descriptions./$defs/configIndex: The local code index caps: file count, per-file bytes, tree bytes, shard-cache bytes, trees kept by prune, and references recorded per file. Absent keys keep the built-in defaults.

descriptions: What the agent writes per prompts/review.md and report --cost rolls up. One object per run, or an array when a bundle was reviewed more than once. The script only sums — it never prices: effort defaults to standard when missing or unknown, records without models still count as runs but not as runs_with_cost, every `models[]` entry must name its model — the name is what attribution reads, and the rollup sums all of them into one total rather than reporting per model, absent/unreadable records contribute zeros and never fail. Per-chunk records (chunks/<name>.cost.json) share this shape. Two readers treat unknown keys differently, and this schema allows them for both. Aggregators — the rollup, the group estimate, the receipt — read the fields they know and ignore the rest, so a newer writer's extra field never voids history. Certification of lens evidence is version-scoped: a record offered as schema_version "2" may carry only the top-level fields v2 defines, and an extra one refuses that record by name until it is removed or a version that defines it is declared. A record bound to the run at a different version refuses as unsupported rather than being re-read as v2.
descriptions./$defs/record/properties/effort: Run tier; missing or unknown values roll up as standard.
descriptions./$defs/record/properties/models: One entry per model that generated tokens: the synthesizer first, then each lens.
descriptions./$defs/record/properties/est_usd: The agent's own math from its price sheet, null when prices are unknown — never guessed.
descriptions./$defs/modelSpend/properties/cache_read_: Input tokens served from cache; a subset of input_tokens, never an addition. Absent or null reads as unknown, never zero.
descriptions./$defs/modelSpend/properties/cache_creat: Input tokens spent writing the cache; a subset of input_tokens, never an addition. Absent or null reads as unknown, never zero.

descriptions: One benchmark corpus manifest, checked in as bench/corpus/<id>/case.json and copied into a run bundle as .verdict/state/corpus-*/corpus.json. The case records the ground truth a review output is graded against: a real PR that later needed a bug-fix commit, or a seeded defect with what was injected. calibrate and trend join findings.json against these bugs offline; a true positive needs the bug's path, a line inside the +/- line_tolerance window, and text that names the defect (kind, category, or keywords), one finding per bug. additionalProperties stays closed so a typo fails validation instead of silently grading a different field.
descriptions./properties/id: Stable case id, matching the bench/corpus/<id> directory name.
descriptions./properties/kind: seeded for deterministic injected fixtures, real for a published PR with a later fix.
descriptions./properties/line_tolerance: How many lines from a bug still count as the same defect (default 1). Keep it narrower than the new-side span of the hunk that shows the bug. A hit is one-to-one: a second finding on the same bug is a false positive.
descriptions./properties/provenance: Where the case came from: injected text for seeded cases, or repo/PR/fix_commit for real ones. The validation test enforces the per-kind requirements the schema cannot express.
descriptions./properties/bugs: At least one known defect. path, line, kind, and severity are the published ground truth; matching uses path, the line window, and the defect the finding names, not severity.
descriptions./$defs/provenance: Case origin. Seeded cases name what was injected; real cases name the repository, PR number, and the later commit that fixed the bug.
descriptions./$defs/bug: One known defect: the reviewed path, the line in the reviewed head, the defect kind (off-by-one, nil-deref, injection, missing-error-check, ...), and the severity a good review should assign.
descriptions./$defs/bug/properties/keywords: Optional phrases a finding may use to name this defect, matched case-insensitively at a word start. kind and the published category vocabulary always name it too, so a case with no keywords still matches.
descriptions./$defs/bug/properties/also_lines: Optional alternate anchors for the same defect: each entry is a new-side line in the same hunk, matched with the same tolerance and defect-naming rule as the primary line. Matching any anchor counts the bug once and reports the primary line.

descriptions: Every --json stdout is exactly one envelope with these nine keys (schema_version "1"): error null on success with a data object, data null with a typed error object on refusal. Derived from the Go envelope renderer (RenderEnvelope) in the verdict CLI. data is additive per verb (chunk summaries, prompt_dump, cost, completeness ride inside data, never as new top-level keys), so data objects allow additional properties; every verb publishes its data profile here as a single <verb>Data $defs entry (reportData, postData, recordData, showData, fetchData, fetchLocalData, threadsData, verifyData, triageData, readyData, adoptData, nextData, fixData, learnData, packData, packTestData, initData, doctorData, checkTreeData, trendData, calibrateData, configData), each validated against the runtime writer and the committed goldens.
descriptions./properties/pr: Numeric PR, else null (local slugs never coerce).
descriptions./$defs/error: Refusal shape from fail(): data is null, message carries the cause plus a try: hint, candidates rides only on the oversize-fetch refusal.
descriptions./$defs/findingItem: Ranked or merged finding locator shared by report items and post/record items.
descriptions./$defs/provenance: Review provenance triple: the tooling behind a run, so mixed-version histories never read as one series. The writer always emits all three keys; model is null when no cost record names one.
descriptions./$defs/reportData: report --json data: ranked read over the store. cost appears only with --cost, completeness only with --completeness, gate only when a gating flag (--max-severity, --require-head, --live) is set (gate itself always carries the coverage dimension), receipt keys only when budget.json parses.
descriptions./$defs/reportCompleteness/properties/sam: True when the reviewed bundle identity and the posted post.json patch id share id and kind (rebase/amend with the same change); absent when either side has no patch id.
descriptions./$defs/reportCompleteness/properties/rev: Patch id the bundle identity carried at review time; absent when the bundle had no identity.
descriptions./$defs/reportCompleteness/properties/pos: Patch id the completed post receipt carried; absent when the post predates patch identity.
descriptions./$defs/reportGate: Composed gate result: every requested dimension in findings, head, coverage, live_threads, compliance order. passed is true iff no dimension failed or read unknown, so a skip and an auto-posture unreachable probe stay neutral.
descriptions./$defs/reportGate/properties/passed: The gate verdict the exit code follows: exit 0 when true, exit 1 when false.
descriptions./$defs/gateDimension: One gate dimension: its id, verdict status, human detail text, and its own failing tally (null where the dimension has no count to report).
descriptions./$defs/gateDimension/properties/id: Which dimension read: findings (open findings at-or-above the --max-severity tier), head (a completed post for the fetched HEAD under --require-head), coverage (the stored diff-coverage receipt for that HEAD under --coverage, default require; a chunked bundle is graded on the chunk attestation its receipt stores), or live_threads (unresolved threads on the PR under --live).
descriptions./$defs/gateDimension/properties/status: pass, fail, unknown (the dimension could not be read and the posture fails closed), or skip (not requested, or unreachable under --live auto). Only fail and unknown fail the gate.
descriptions./$defs/gateDimension/properties/count: The dimension's own tally: offending findings for findings, unattested ranges for coverage (unattested chunks on a chunked bundle), versus-thread count for live_threads, null for head and for a skipped or unreachable live probe.
descriptions./$defs/reportCost: Summed rollup from cost.json plus per-chunk records; by_tier always carries all three tiers.
descriptions./$defs/reportCost/properties/cached_inpu: Summed per-model cache_read_input_tokens plus cache_creation_input_tokens; totals stay input + output exactly.
descriptions./$defs/postData: post --dry-run --json data (dry_run true, findings carry the dry-run file) and real-post data (dry_run false, findings carry counts plus the accepted review object).
descriptions./$defs/postData/properties/review: Real-post only: the accepted GitHub review object.
descriptions./$defs/recordData: record --json data: the local-bundle merge (post stays refused, no PR target).
descriptions./$defs/showData: show --json data: item is the raw finding record in store key order; fix is the read-only machine repair directive built from that record plus the bundle's patch/verification history. Neither key adds execution, flags, or store writes.
descriptions./$defs/serveData: serve --json data (and the start envelope): one profile across health, roots, inbox, detail, and the start line, so every view-specific key is optional while partial, sources, and errors are always present. A product refusal is data null with the typed error; a corrupt bundle in a listing keeps its row with null counts and an errors[] entry, and any total over it is null and partial.
descriptions./$defs/serveData/properties/via: The detector that found this invalidation: tick for directory stamps or sweep for entry fingerprints.
descriptions./$defs/serveData/properties/changed: Bundle names whose views should be fetched again; a truncated event requires refetching the full inbox.
descriptions./$defs/serveData/properties/removed: Bundle names removed from the served root.
descriptions./$defs/serveSource: One artifact a composed view read: the serving root id, the bundle name (empty for a root-level override fragment), the root-relative slash path, its SHA-256, and the byte count. Every inventory read is capped.
descriptions./$defs/serveErrorRow: One tolerated bundle failure: the root id, bundle name, machine code, and message. A row is never dropped for a refused bundle.
descriptions./$defs/serveRoot: One served root: its 12-hex id, absolute path, and addressable bundle count.
descriptions./$defs/serveCounts: The portfolio rollup over the inbox rows. Null when any input bundle refuses, so a partial set never reads as a smaller total.
descriptions./$defs/serveRow: One inbox row: the bundle identity, its post receipt's model, and the verdict counts. Every numeric count is null for a refused bundle, never zero-for-unknown.
descriptions./$defs/serveArtifact: One evidence-ledger row: the bundle-relative path, its presence, and the hash and size when present.
descriptions./$defs/serveCache: The in-memory composition cache's size; derived state only, never written to disk.
descriptions./$defs/serveSkipped: Discovery counts directory symlinks not followed and unsupported .gitignore patterns skipped.
descriptions./$defs/serveDiscovery: Whether the root list came from the registry. S1 reports cached false with an empty scanned_at.
descriptions./$defs/serveCostData: A cost view for one allowlisted dimension. Model rows carry tokens but no per-model price; corrupt inputs make totals null and partial true.
descriptions./$defs/serveCostBucket: One repository, ISO week, or model bucket. runs counts record membership; model_runs counts model entries, which can be greater than runs for by=model.
descriptions./$defs/serveCostTotals: The rollup for a cost view. est_usd is null for by=model because cost records price only the whole run.
descriptions./$defs/serveCostBucket/properties/input_: Null when any contributing model has no input-token measurement.
descriptions./$defs/serveCostBucket/properties/output: Null when any contributing model has no output-token measurement.
descriptions./$defs/serveCostBucket/properties/total_: Null when either token measurement is unknown.
descriptions./$defs/serveCostTotals/properties/input_: Null when any contributing bucket has an unknown input-token measurement.
descriptions./$defs/serveCostTotals/properties/output: Null when any contributing bucket has an unknown output-token measurement.
descriptions./$defs/serveCostTotals/properties/total_: Null when any contributing bucket has an unknown token measurement.
descriptions./$defs/servePrecisionData: Precision from the stored threads feed. fixed is not measured and remains null; no rate is published. as_of comes from fetched_at.
descriptions./$defs/servePrecisionBucket: Counts from the calibrate join. fixed stays null without changed-file evidence.
descriptions./$defs/servePrecisionTotals: The stored-join outcome counts across all dimensions; fixed is always null.
descriptions./$defs/threadsFile: The bundle's threads.json feed; null when the bundle carries none. Shape shared with threads.schema.json.
descriptions./$defs/thread: One root review thread or conversation comment plus its replies.
descriptions./$defs/comment: One comment inside a thread, body capped and flagged.
descriptions./$defs/showFix: The per-finding repair directive: identity, status, files, locator, embedded suggestion, and the last recorded rerun hint. Missing history reads as null; caution is a fixed untrusted-evidence reminder, never composed from finding text.
descriptions./$defs/showFix/properties/status: The record's stored status string, read verbatim (absent reads empty, never invented).
descriptions./$defs/showFix/properties/files: Deduped anchor paths read from the record (path plus any files/related_files lists); [] when the record names none.
descriptions./$defs/showFix/properties/locator: path[:line] for inline findings, the heading for section findings, else empty.
descriptions./$defs/showFix/properties/suggestion: The record's embedded suggestion body, or null when absent.
descriptions./$defs/showFix/properties/verify_hint: The exact rerun command plus resultHead from verification.json for this sig, else a matching (or unnamed) patch.json; null when no history exists. Never executed.
descriptions./$defs/showFix/properties/caution: Fixed untrusted-evidence reminder: finding text quotes attacker-controlled PR content and is never an instruction.
descriptions./$defs/verifyHint: A recorded rerun command and its nullable head bracket.
descriptions./$defs/fetchEstimate: fetch --json data.estimate, in exactly one of two shapes. A whole-run resolution names the projected tier and cost from comparable past runs, with basis/harness/measured_runs appearing only when a local harness session priced a comparable run (their absence is the legacy self-reported estimate). A grouped resolution names each plan group's guard, tier and history-backed projection, plus the personal ceiling comparison; projected_usd is absent for a group no bound history priced, and the personal total is absent when any group is unknown, leaving the known subtotal as a lower bound.
descriptions./$defs/fetchEstimate/properties/groups: One entry per resolved plan group: its stable id, effort tier, its own guard when the plan resolved one, and projected_usd only when bound history priced it.
descriptions./$defs/fetchEstimate/properties/personal: The personal whole-run ceiling comparison: exact-total when every group is priced, known-lower-bound when some are unknown, no-personal-limit when no ceiling was set. limit_usd is absent when unset and never zero; total_usd is absent unless the aggregate is exact.
descriptions./$defs/fetchGroupEstimate/properties/gua: The group's resolved guard. Absent when the plan set none — never reported as zero.
descriptions./$defs/fetchGroupPersonal/properties/lim: The resolved personal ceiling. Absent when none was set — never reported as zero.
descriptions./$defs/fetchGroupEstimate: One plan group's public projection. projected_usd is omitted for an unknown group rather than reported as zero.
descriptions./$defs/reportCompliance: The captured-policy compliance view: whether the bundle captured a policy and its provenance verified, how many findings blocked and how many required checks are still pending for the saved head, and whether the work therefore satisfies the policy. Unknown or pending never reads as satisfied.
descriptions./$defs/reportCompliance/properties/block: Blocking findings under the captured clauses; never negative.
descriptions./$defs/reportCompliance/properties/confl: Applicable clauses whose reviewed material is withheld by an accepted privacy exclusion, so the clause cannot be satisfied by absence of findings; never negative.
descriptions./$defs/reportCompliance/properties/pendi: Required checks still pending for the saved head; never negative.
descriptions./$defs/reportCompliance/properties/gaps: Accepted conflicts and pending required work counted together as the standing gap tally; never negative.
descriptions./$defs/fetchGroupPersonal: The personal ceiling comparison. total_usd appears only with an exact aggregate, known_subtotal_usd only as a lower bound.
descriptions./$defs/fetchEstimate/properties/basis: measured when every priced sample in the projected tier was harness-measured, mixed when only some were. Absent means no harness measurement contributed.
descriptions./$defs/fetchEstimate/properties/harness: Measured session sources behind the projection (e.g. claude-code, opencode); absent with basis.
descriptions./$defs/fetchEstimate/properties/measured: How many priced samples in the projected tier came from a harness session; absent with basis.
descriptions./$defs/showFix/properties/brief: The stored machine brief, read as stored without re-validation, or null when the finding has none.
descriptions./$defs/brief: The machine form of the finding: affected sites, the required outcome, an optional approach, and open questions.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/sites: Affected changed files with an optional reviewed line; a site outside every hunk warns and drops.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/outcome: One sentence naming what the fix must achieve — required, 10–500 characters.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/questions: Optional questions for the human, at most 10 of 10–300 characters each.
descriptions./$defs/briefSite/properties/line: Reviewed line inside a hunk; absent means the whole file.
descriptions./$defs/triageData: triage --json data: the finding that moved and its new status. dry_run appears only when the pass changed nothing.
descriptions./$defs/readyData: ready --json data: the gate verdict, every blocker with the action that clears it, and the live PR state the gate read. recommendation is review when nothing blocks, hold otherwise.
descriptions./$defs/readyBlocker: One readiness blocker: the rule that fired, the detail that fired it, and the action that clears it.
descriptions./$defs/readyCI: The live CI check tally: failing rows out of every check the head reported.
descriptions./$defs/adoptData: adopt --json data: the target bundle, its source, and how many findings were adopted and left open.
descriptions./$defs/nextData: next --json data: the ranked finding to fix next, or null when the store has nothing open. item keeps every stored record key beside the ranked locator.
descriptions./$defs/fixData: fix --json data: one pass over the named finding, or the completion shape. The pass carries the finding identity, its anchors, the pass budget, and the open/fixed/stopped tallies; completion leaves those null and sets complete.
descriptions./$defs/fixAnchors: The pass's anchor block, read verbatim from the record (line and start_line stay strings).
descriptions./$defs/learnData: learn --json data: exactly one of rule (one appended rule) or rules (the status listing).
descriptions./$defs/packData: pack list --json data: one row per loaded pack in precedence order (built-in, org, repo).
descriptions./$defs/packEntry: One pack row: its manifest identity, layer, source, canonical tree hash, declared lens and rule ids, and drift (null when a repo pack matches verdict.lock, else pack-lock-missing or pack-lock-drift; built-in and org rows are never locked).
descriptions./$defs/packAddData: pack add --json data: the added pack row as it now lists from the repo layer, whether it replaced an existing entry, and the previous tree hash (null on a first add).
descriptions./$defs/packTestData: pack test --json data: the resolved pack name, one PASS, SKIP, or FAIL row per sorted eval case, and the status counts.
descriptions./$defs/packTestCase: One offline pack eval case and its result. A reason is present for SKIP and FAIL.
descriptions./$defs/packTestSummary: Counts the passing, skipped, and failing pack eval cases.
descriptions./$defs/initData: init --json data: the applied preset values and the files they were written to.
descriptions./$defs/doctorData: doctor --json data: every preflight row and the healthy verdict over them. Row values are environment-shaped, so the goldens, not this schema, pin them.
descriptions./$defs/doctorCheck: One preflight row: the check name, its severity, whether it passed, and the observed detail.
descriptions./$defs/checkTreeData: check-tree --json data: the clean verdict plus exactly one of four explanations — ignored_review_lines (clean, with ignored .verdict/state paths), files (dirty), expected_only (only expected paths changed), unexpected (unexpected paths changed).
descriptions./$defs/verifyData: verify --json data: the command's exit status, whether the watchdog timed it out, the redacted output tail, the patch read back from the bundle, and whether the run was sandboxed (absent means unsandboxed). A timed-out run is never proof.
descriptions./$defs/trendData: trend --json data: the portfolio rollup, one row per reviewed bundle, and the opt-in overlap and corpus joins. Every tally key is always present.
descriptions./$defs/trendStatuses: A five-status finding tally: open, addressed, wont-fix, false-positive, deferred.
descriptions./$defs/trendTiers: A four-tier finding tally: critical, important, informational, untagged.
descriptions./$defs/trendProvenance: The distinct tools, models, and prompt hashes behind the rollup; a bundle that recorded none contributes a null entry.
descriptions./$defs/trendPeriod: One time bucket of the rollup, with the same tallies as the whole.
descriptions./$defs/trendBundleRow: One reviewed bundle's contribution: its model/effort inventory, provenance triple, status and tier tallies, and bundle-local counts.
descriptions./$defs/provenanceTriple: The per-bundle tooling triple; any part the bundle never recorded reads null rather than an empty string.
descriptions./$defs/calibrateData: calibrate --json data: one object shared by the three modes, so every mode-specific key is optional. The live join fills review_id, head, pr, outcomes, precision (an object with by_tier), and provenance; the corpus join fills bundle, case, kind, model, panel, line_tolerance, ground_truth, reported, matched, false_positives, missed, precision (a rate or null), recall, false_positive_rate, outcomes, and missed_bugs; the probe fills bundle, grades, counts, and judgment.
descriptions./$defs/calibrateHead: The reviewed and live head the live join compared.
descriptions./$defs/calibratePR: The live PR state the join read; merged_at is null until the PR merges.
descriptions./$defs/calibrateCounts: The probe's verdict tally over the bundle's findings: how many graded real, false, or unknown.
descriptions./$defs/calibrateJudgment: The probe's second-sample agreement tally; agreement_rate is null until at least one finding is judged.
descriptions./$defs/fetchData: fetch --json data: the bundle location, the diff statistics the toc counted, the panel, and the conditional summaries the run armed. estimate and budget travel together, cap and chunk follow only when armed, and prompt_dump lands last when staged.
descriptions./$defs/fetchLocalData: fetch-local --json data: the same statistics without a remote base, plus the worktree kind and no incremental_base.
descriptions./$defs/fetchPanel: The panel source (null when unpinned) and its member list.
descriptions./$defs/fetchCapabilities: What verdict can do through one host's own CLI or API: the boolean table an agent plans with, the compatibility sum review_verdicts, and one machine-readable reason per absent capability.
descriptions./$defs/fetchCapabilities/properties/revi: approve && request_changes, kept so a consumer written before the split reads the same truth; new readers branch on approve and request_changes.
descriptions./$defs/fetchCapabilities/properties/unsu: One machine-readable reason code per absent capability, keyed by capability name. Only an absent capability appears; a host that carries everything carries an empty object.
descriptions./$defs/fetchData/properties/artifacts: Bundle file paths by name (PR.json, full.diff, toc.txt, roles.txt, reviews.json, inline.json, threads.json, sensitive.txt, incremental.diff, plus kb.txt and kb-recall.json when present); files the run did not write read null.
descriptions./$defs/fetchData/properties/controls: The review controls the run read from controls.json; shape owned by the controls document.
descriptions./$defs/fetchData/properties/budget: The resolved budget summary; present when the run resolved an ordinary budget (a grouped run reports its per-group guards and personal ceiling under estimate instead).
descriptions./$defs/fetchData/properties/cap: The armed cost cap summary; absent when no cap is armed.
descriptions./$defs/fetchData/properties/chunk: The chunk plan summary; absent when the run was not chunked.
descriptions./$defs/fetchData/properties/prompt_dump: Where the staged prompt was written; absent unless a dump was requested.
descriptions./$defs/threadsData: threads --json data: where the refreshed feed was written plus a tally over it. The feed document itself is threads.schema.json.
descriptions./$defs/threadsResolveData: threads resolve --json data: the receipt path, the host and head it proves, the ids it closed, and the candidates it left open with a reason. A dry run carries the same plan with dry_run true and writes nothing.
descriptions./$defs/threadsResolveSkip: One candidate a resolve run left open: its host thread id and the machine-readable reason (already-resolved, no-finding-link, finding-not-addressed).
descriptions./$defs/fetchLocalData/properties/control: The review controls the run read from controls.json; shape owned by the controls document.
descriptions./$defs/fetchLocalData/properties/artifac: Bundle file paths by name (PR.json, full.diff, toc.txt, roles.txt, reviews.json, inline.json, threads.json, sensitive.txt, incremental.diff, plus kb.txt and kb-recall.json when present); files the run did not write read null.
descriptions./$defs/fetchLocalData/properties/budget: The resolved budget summary; present when the run resolved an ordinary budget (a grouped run reports its per-group guards and personal ceiling under estimate instead).
descriptions./$defs/fetchLocalData/properties/cap: The armed cost cap summary; absent when no cap is armed.
descriptions./$defs/fetchLocalData/properties/chunk: The chunk plan summary; absent when the run was not chunked.
descriptions./$defs/fetchLocalData/properties/prompt_: Where the staged prompt was written; absent unless a dump was requested.
descriptions./$defs/error/properties/problems: Review-input problems in document order, errors first (at most 50); present on a bad-review-input refusal and on a repair-exhausted refusal, with the exact fix for each.
descriptions./$defs/error/properties/problems_truncat: How many problems were past the 50-problem cap; 0 when the list is complete.
descriptions./$defs/problem: One review-input problem: its JSONPath in review.json, the published code, the level, the message, the exact fix, and an optional example of the accepted shape. --strict and controls strict_input promote warnings to errors.
descriptions./$defs/problem/properties/code: Published problem-code enum; the envelope error.code stays bad-review-input.
descriptions./$defs/problem/properties/level: error blocks record; warning lets it proceed and report what it did, unless strict input promotes it.
descriptions./$defs/problem/properties/fix: The exact change that clears the problem.
descriptions./$defs/problem/properties/example: Optional example of the accepted shape at this path.
descriptions./$defs/checkSummary: What a clean dry run would record: comment and section counts plus anchors that would move to the body.
descriptions./$defs/recordData/properties/dry_run: True only on record --dry-run; the run wrote no findings.json, record.json, or any new file.
descriptions./$defs/recordData/properties/check: Present only on a clean dry run: the review-input summary.
descriptions./$defs/recordData/properties/normalized: Present on record --dry-run: the exact review object the checker read after safe repairs, as an object.
descriptions./$defs/recordData/properties/repairs: Present on record --dry-run: every safe review.json rewrite applied, in document order.
descriptions./$defs/repair: One safe review.json rewrite: the published repair code and the JSONPath it touched.
descriptions./$defs/repair/properties/code: The repair family: fence unwrap, prose extraction, scalar-to-array, key alias, enum synonym, or trivia removal.
descriptions./$defs/repair/properties/path: JSONPath of the repaired value in the normalized review.
descriptions./$defs/reportCounts/properties/by_catego: Whole-store finding counts by published category plus untagged; every key is always present with zero defaults.
descriptions./$defs/reportFilters/properties/category: The active --category filter, or null when the run did not filter by category.
descriptions./$defs/trendData/properties/by_category: Portfolio finding counts by observed category with untagged for null entries; only observed categories appear.
descriptions./$defs/trendBundleRow/properties/by_cate: One bundle's finding counts by observed category with untagged for null entries.
descriptions./$defs/calibrateData/properties/precisio: Live-join precision: totals plus by_tier counts and by_category cells (fixed, resolved_unfixed, open, unknown, judged, resolution_rate; a zero judged denominator reads null). Outcome rows carry the finding's category, null when untagged.
descriptions./$defs/indexData: index --json data: one object across build, status, prune, callers, tests-for, co-changed, owners, and blast-radius, so kind names the subcommand and every other key is optional.
descriptions./$defs/indexShards: The local shard store: file count and byte total.
descriptions./$defs/indexTreeRow: One stored tree file: its tree SHA, file count, and bytes.
descriptions./$defs/indexRemoved: The prune receipt: trees and shards removed.
descriptions./$defs/indexQuery: The query input: the symbol as written for callers or tests-for --symbol, or the repository path for tests-for, co-changed, and owners.
descriptions./$defs/indexStatus: The queried tree's index state, published by callers and tests-for: tree, commit, staleness, and file coverage.
descriptions./$defs/indexCoverage: The indexed and skipped file counts for the queried tree.
descriptions./$defs/indexCounts: The query counts for the kind: caller rows and candidates left unresolved, candidate tests, or co-change partners and the commits that touched the target.
descriptions./$defs/indexRow: One row of a caller, candidate-test, or co-change query: path plus the fields that kind measures (line/kind/resolution for callers, via for candidates, commits/jaccard for partners).
descriptions./$defs/indexWindow: The bounded history window a co-change query read: oldest and newest commit sha, and how many commits it counted (empty window names no bounds).
descriptions./$defs/indexTarget: One queried path and its CODEOWNERS answer. owners is null when the tree has no CODEOWNERS file (owners_source is null too) or when no rule matches (owners_source names the file); a matching ownerless rule cleared an earlier match, so owners is [] with owners_source named. Never an owner named nobody.
descriptions./$defs/indexBlastInput: blast-radius's query input: the fetched PR bundle slug and its head when --pr read one (both null for --paths), and the resolved changed paths — every path the bundle diff names, or every --paths entry.
descriptions./$defs/indexBlastSymbols: The changed declarations: each declaration whose span the diff touched, or every declaration in a --paths file. count is how many were measured and truncated is how many the limit hid; both are null when no index answered, never 0.
descriptions./$defs/indexBlastSymbol: One changed declaration: the indexed file, the declared name and kind, and its first line. A declaration owns its source from that line to the line before the next declaration.
descriptions./$defs/indexBlastCallers: The callers of the changed declarations within depth 2, walked once per target and deduplicated by call site. count, unresolved, and truncated are null when no index answered.
descriptions./$defs/indexBlastCaller: One caller row: the changed symbol it is reached from (import path and name), the call site, and the depth — 1 for a direct caller, 2 for a caller of a direct caller. resolution is exact within the declaring package and lexical through an import edge, as `index callers` defines it.
descriptions./$defs/indexBlastTests: The candidate tests to read for the changed declarations, strongest mechanism per file. A candidate is never a coverage claim, and count/truncated are null when no index answered.
descriptions./$defs/indexBlastPartners: The paths that moved with each changed path in one bounded co-change window, read at HEAD. count is the number of (changed path, partner) rows and partners the distinct partner paths across them; truncated is always measured: history needs no index.
descriptions./$defs/indexBlastPartner: One partner path, the changed path it moved with, its co-change count, and the Jaccard ratio.
descriptions./$defs/indexBlastOwners: One ownership row per changed path, from the CODEOWNERS file at the queried tree. count and truncated are always measured.
descriptions./$defs/indexData/properties/index: Present only when the queried tree has a stored index; blast-radius omits it when the symbol, caller, and test lists are unmeasured.

descriptions: What post/record write per bundle. Derived from validate_and_merge in the verdict CLI: stable line-number-free sigs, append-only history, re-post merges that keep prior fields ($prev + new, so unknown keys pass through — this schema allows them). rigor is always normalized to the enum, severity and category to the enum-or-null (unknown category values warn and read null), kb defaults to []. Section entries carry anchored:"body" instead of a boolean.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/sig: Stable cross-run join key: SHA-1 of path + heading + body, whitespace-squashed.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/sig_version: Normalization generation; backfilled onto older entries, never clobbered.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/heading: Section findings only: the exact ### body heading.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/anchored: Inline: true when the anchor sits inside one reviewed hunk. Section: the string "body".
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/kb: Cited knowledge-base rule ids; [] when uncited.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/inBounds: CamelCase in the store (hyphenated in review.json input); absent reads true.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/rigor: Evidence rung on inline findings; the re-post merge stamps an explicit null onto section entries.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/history: Append-only: reported, claim, reopened, revalidation, addressed, triaged.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/brief: Optional machine brief; excluded from the sig, and preserved across re-record when the fresh comment carries none.
descriptions./$defs/brief: The machine form of the finding: affected sites, the required outcome, an optional approach, and open questions.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/sites: Affected changed files with an optional reviewed line; a site outside every hunk warns and drops.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/outcome: One sentence naming what the fix must achieve — required, 10–500 characters.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/questions: Optional questions for the human, at most 10 of 10–300 characters each.
descriptions./$defs/briefSite/properties/line: Reviewed line inside a hunk; absent means the whole file.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/rigor_source: Where the recorded rung came from: model when the review set it, default when the checker filled said, verified reserved for later.
descriptions./$defs/entry/properties/category: Optional agent-supplied taxonomy; absent and null group as untagged in report, calibrate, and trend. Never part of the sig.

descriptions: Written only by the real-post path in the verdict CLI (dry runs, attempts and failures write nothing), so a present head matching the bundle HEAD proves a completed post. review is raw GitHub output (GitHub's schema, unversioned) — this schema passes it through. confidence/security_summary are absent-stays-absent: null when the review carried none. additionalProperties stays open for additive provenance fields.
descriptions./properties/review: Raw GitHub review object: id, html_url and whatever the API returned.
descriptions./properties/head: Reviewed commit SHA; doubles as the single-review finalizer key.
descriptions./properties/posted_at: UTC timestamp of the completed post.
descriptions./properties/tool_version: Tool version that wrote this record (from package.json).
descriptions./properties/prompts_hash: sha256 over the sorted prompt-set file names plus contents (SKILL.md plus prompts/system.md, prompts/review.md, prompts/diagrams.md).
descriptions./properties/model: First model of the latest cost record, else null when no cost record names one.
descriptions./properties/patch_id: Bundle patch id the post reviewed, copied from identity.json; absent when the bundle had no identity.
descriptions./properties/patch_id_kind: Patch id algorithm (git-patch-id or the labeled diff-sha256 fallback); absent when the bundle had no identity.
descriptions./properties/forced: One entry per guard --force bypassed, in guard order; absent when the post needed no override.
descriptions./properties/withheld: One entry per capability the host could not carry, in the order the run discovered it: a GitLab REQUEST_CHANGES recorded as a comment lands here while review.state reads commented. Absent when every capability the run asked for landed.
descriptions./properties/secret_shapes_allowed: Published value-shape names --allow-secret-values let through, one per distinct shape the review text carried; absent when the flag allowed nothing, so an unflagged receipt keeps its bytes.
descriptions./$defs/withheldCapability: One capability a host withheld from the post that landed, with the reason code data.capabilities publishes for it.
descriptions./$defs/withheldCapability/properties/cap: Published capability name (post, inline_anchors, approve, request_changes, thread_resolution) — the same string data.capabilities.unsupported keys.
descriptions./$defs/withheldCapability/properties/rea: Published reason code for the gap (fetch-only, no-request-changes-event, no-approve-verdict, no-inline-anchors, no-resolve-mutation, unknown-host); docs/manual.md § Providers maps each code to its sentence.
descriptions./$defs/withheldCapability/properties/req: Binding verdict the run asked for, spelled as the envelope's event (APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES); absent for a capability with no event of its own, whose loss the anchors tally counts.
descriptions./$defs/forcedPost: One explicit --force bypass: the fired guard plus the prior bundle and head when a same-patch sibling refused.
descriptions./$defs/forcedPost/properties/patch_id: Patch id the refused sibling shared, for the same-patch bypass; else null.
descriptions./$defs/forcedPost/properties/previous_bu: Sibling bundle slug the bypass overrode, for the same-patch bypass; else null.
descriptions./$defs/forcedPost/properties/previous_he: Prior reviewed head the bypass overrode, for same-SHA and same-patch bypasses; else null.

descriptions: Bundle patch identity written by fetch/fetch-local beside the diff: the stable diff id (git patch-id --stable, labeled diff-sha256 fallback) with the head/base SHAs it was computed at. A patch id is a dedupe key, never an authorization token.
descriptions./properties/patch_id: Stable patch id, or null for an empty diff; a fallback id never matches a git-patch-id value.
descriptions./properties/patch_id_kind: Patch id algorithm: git-patch-id, the labeled diff-sha256 fallback, or none for an empty diff.
descriptions./properties/diff_sha256: SHA-256 of the bundle full.diff (the filtered store hash).
descriptions./properties/raw_diff_sha256: SHA-256 of the identity input (full.raw.diff when present, else full.diff).
descriptions./properties/head_sha: Bundle head SHA the diff was computed at.
descriptions./properties/base_sha: Bundle base SHA the diff was computed at.

descriptions: The repo layer's pin file at .verdict/verdict.lock: strict JSON with exactly one row per pack vendored under .verdict/packs/, sorted by name. The lock covers only the repo layer — the built-in pack is pinned by the binary and org packs live in per-operator settings. source is dir:<path as given> or git:<allowlisted url>@<40-hex sha>; hash is the pack's canonical tree hash; sig is sha256 over name, source, version, and hash, so a hand edit is caught. fetch, post, and record refuse pack-lock-missing or pack-lock-drift from the trusted-base snapshot, and the file joins the controls inventory so an edited snapshot copy refuses controls-stale.
descriptions./properties/packs: One pinned pack row per vendored repo pack, sorted by name.
descriptions./$defs/pack: One pinned pack: its manifest identity, where it was vendored from, the canonical tree hash, and an integrity digest over those fields.
descriptions./$defs/pack/properties/name: Manifest pack identity as <namespace>/<slug>; the vendored directory is the slug.
descriptions./$defs/pack/properties/source: dir:<path as given on the add command line> or git:<url>@<resolved 40-hex HEAD sha>. A dir: payload is a slash path with no control character, backslash, or leading "-". A git: URL is exactly https://host/path with no userinfo, ssh://user@host/path, or user@host:path, with a DNS, IPv4, or bracketed IPv6 host, a path with no control character, whitespace, "?", "#", or leading "-", and only the bare [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} ssh user; the scheme is stored lower-case, so an upper-case row refuses.
descriptions./$defs/pack/properties/version: Pinned pack semver, as the manifest declares it.
descriptions./$defs/pack/properties/hash: The pack's canonical tree hash: sha256 over sorted slash paths, each fed as `== <path-length>:<path> ==`, the body's byte length, the body's bytes, then a newline.
descriptions./$defs/pack/properties/sig: sha256 over the entry's name, source, version, and hash in that order, one `key=value` line each. Integrity only: a hand edit breaks it; it is not a signature.

descriptions: A lens pack manifest at skills/verdict/packs/builtin/pack.json: the published format fetch resolves into the bundle. The schema closes the shape; the loader also enforces the caps (64 KiB/file, 1 MiB/pack, 256 files, 64 lenses) and the rule that every lens and rule id names its own markdown file. A file no manifest row names is counted but never loaded. Manifest keys must be spelled exactly as published: the loader refuses any other case.
descriptions./properties/name: Pack identity as <namespace>/<slug>, for example verdict/builtin.
descriptions./properties/version: Pack semver; fetch prints <name>@<version> on every plan group line.
descriptions./properties/replace: Lower-layer pack names this pack may override by id. Replacement is downward only: naming a pack at the same or a higher layer refuses pack-conflict.
descriptions./properties/severity: The pack's severity names mapped to critical, important, or informational; every rule's severity key must exist here.
descriptions./properties/lenses: One row per lens, at least one; the loader refuses more than 64 with pack-too-large. Each id names lenses/<id>.md.
descriptions./properties/rules: One row per KB rule; each id names rules/<id>.md, globs are required, and the severity key resolves through this pack's severity map.
descriptions./$defs/lens: One lens row: its id, optional group-file globs, and the dispatch caps. A lens with no globs is offered for every plan group; a lens whose globs match none of a group's files is not offered for that group.
descriptions./$defs/rule: One rule row: a KB id, the severity-map key that resolves its level, required scope globs, and the tools it talks about.
descriptions./$defs/rule/properties/id: KB id grammar: a lowercase slug of at most 65 characters; the body is rules/<id>.md.
descriptions./$defs/rule/properties/severity: Key into the manifest severity map; the mapped value is the rule's published severity.
descriptions./$defs/rule/properties/globs: Required slash-path globs; a rule that matches no changed file is not recalled.
descriptions./$defs/rule/properties/tools: Optional tool names the rule talks about.
descriptions./$defs/lens/properties/id: Lowercase slug; the body is lenses/<id>.md and the file stem must equal the id.
descriptions./$defs/lens/properties/globs: Optional slash-path globs matched with the repository-config dialect; absent means every plan group.
descriptions./$defs/lens/properties/max_files: Dispatch scope cap, 1..24 files; the shipped reviewer contract states at most ~12.
descriptions./$defs/lens/properties/max_findings: Dispatch return cap, 1..20 findings; the shipped reviewer contract states at most 10.

descriptions: Written by the record verb in the verdict CLI for local and provider-PR bundles (GitHub PRs use post). findings/open are recomputed from the merged store every run; confidence/security_summary are null when the review carried none. additionalProperties stays open for additive provenance fields.
descriptions./properties/status: Bundle provider that was recorded (e.g. local).
descriptions./properties/head: Reviewed SHA (real head_sha, or "dirty"/"unknown" when the bundle has none).
descriptions./properties/diff_sha256: SHA-256 of full.diff at record time.
descriptions./properties/recorded_at: UTC timestamp of the record run.
descriptions./properties/tool_version: Tool version that wrote this record (from package.json).
descriptions./properties/prompts_hash: sha256 over the sorted prompt-set file names plus contents (SKILL.md plus prompts/system.md, prompts/review.md, prompts/diagrams.md).
descriptions./properties/model: First model of the latest cost record, else null when no cost record names one.
descriptions./properties/repairs: Safe review.json rewrites applied before the merge, in document order; absent when the review was already clean.
descriptions./properties/patch_id: Bundle patch id at record time, copied from identity.json; absent when the bundle had no identity.
descriptions./properties/patch_id_kind: Patch id algorithm (git-patch-id or the labeled diff-sha256 fallback); absent when the bundle had no identity.

descriptions: What the agent writes and post/record validate. One checker reports every problem: error refuses; warning lets record proceed and is promoted by --strict/strict_input. Errors: schema_version other than 1, missing/non-string/degenerate body, non-boolean approved, non-array comments or non-object items, comment path missing/non-string/not in diff, line/start_line wrong type, side wrong type or not RIGHT/LEFT, missing body, non-string suggestion, brief outcome/site/approach/question shape or range failures, rigor/severity wrong type or unknown, non-boolean in-bounds, kb non-array/non-string, resolved/triage/sections shape and enums, confidence non-integer or outside 1-5, non-string security_summary, malformed or partial chunks, and malformed verification claims. Warnings: missing schema_version, missing comments, no line/start_line, anchor outside hunks, unknown fields, unset rigor, an unknown or non-string category (warns once, stores null), brief site outside hunks, fenced suggestion, malformed kb id, and unknown or unattested chunks. Unknown top-level keys are allowed by the schema but still warn.
descriptions./properties/schema_version: Agents stamp "1"; missing warns, any other value refuses.
descriptions./properties/body: Full review text, verdict marker first line. Missing, non-string, or degenerate text (<20 chars with no verdict marker, or a short placeholder) refuses.
descriptions./properties/approved: Binding ask; the CLI --bind/--request-changes flags win over this. A non-boolean refuses.
descriptions./properties/comments: Inline findings; one per anchor. Missing warns as an empty list; a non-array or non-object item refuses.
descriptions./properties/resolved: Finding sigs (full or unambiguous prefix) the run addresses. Bare claims only record history; addressed needs verification.json evidence. A non-array or non-string item refuses.
descriptions./properties/triage: Status claims with rationale. Unknown status refuses the run; unknown sig warns; rationale under 30 chars keeps the prior status. Shape and enum failures refuse.
descriptions./properties/sections: Severity tags for ### body sections; exact heading string, unmatched tags ignored. Shape and enum failures refuse.
descriptions./properties/confidence: Review-level certainty, integer 1-5; a non-integer or out-of-range value refuses.
descriptions./properties/security_summary: One-paragraph security read; a non-string value refuses.
descriptions./properties/chunks: Coverage attestation on chunked bundles: every manifest chunk name the synthesis covers. Missing warns; non-array/non-string entries and attested-but-partial coverage refuse.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/path: Diff-relative path required; a path not in the fetched diff refuses.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/line: NEW-side line; numeric strings anchor like integers. An absent line/start_line warns and moves the comment to the body; a present non-numeric line warns and keeps it; other types refuse.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/start_line: Multi-line range start with the same tolerance as line: absent warns and moves, non-numeric warns and keeps, other types refuse.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/side: Defaults to RIGHT; LEFT for deleted lines. Any other value refuses.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/suggestion: A fenced suggestion warns and demotes to the body (a fence inside would break rendering); a non-string value refuses.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/rigor: Evidence rung; absent warns (rigor-unset) and records as said with rigor_source default, unknown or non-string values refuse.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/severity: Stored at write time; unknown or non-string values refuse.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/in-bounds: Hyphenated in agent input; absent reads true, a non-boolean refuses.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/kb: Cited knowledge-base rule ids; a non-array or non-string entry refuses, and a malformed id warns and drops.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/brief: Optional machine brief. Shape, type, required-field, and range failures refuse; a site outside every hunk, past a cap, or a short approach/question warns and drops only that part.
descriptions./$defs/brief: The machine form of the finding: affected sites, the required outcome, an optional approach, and open questions.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/sites: Affected changed files with an optional reviewed line. Site shape/type/line failures refuse; a site outside every hunk or past the 10-site cap warns and drops.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/outcome: One sentence naming what the fix must achieve — required, 10–500 characters; missing, non-string, or out-of-range refuses the review.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/approach: Optional suggested approach, 10–1,000 characters; a non-string or out-of-range value refuses.
descriptions./$defs/brief/properties/questions: Optional questions for the human, at most 10 of 10–300 characters each; non-array/non-string or an out-of-range or past-cap question refuses.
descriptions./$defs/briefSite/properties/line: Reviewed line inside a hunk; absent means the whole file.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/category: Optional closed taxonomy: logic|edge-case|security|performance|accidental-commit|style|docs|other. Unknown or non-string values warn once and store null; never inferred from prose, path, severity, or rule. Explicit null clears a stored label on re-post; absent preserves it.

descriptions: One provider bundle's normalized PR-conversation feed, written beside the raw host files (inline.json/reviews.json keep their exact bytes). Each host's native review data is filtered the way its review surface expects (system/deleted/pending comments dropped, host resolution and stale-anchor state read from the host's own fields) and flattened to one shape, so re-review, address-reviews, merge readiness, and calibration read prior feedback without parsing six formats. Review threads are authoritative: GitHub comes from GraphQL reviewThreads (REST has no resolution), GitLab from discussions (resolved/resolvable), Azure from thread status, Forgejo from review-comment resolver/position, Bitbucket from comment resolution + inline.outdated, GitCafe from its comment flags. Unknown root keys are rejected: a new field is a contract change.
descriptions./properties/schema_version: Feed format version; only "1" is read.
descriptions./properties/provider: The host whose raw payload produced this feed.
descriptions./properties/pr: Pull request number the feed belongs to (0 when the positional was not numeric).
descriptions./properties/head_sha: The PR head the feed was read at; GitLab and Forgejo compare it to a comment's anchor commit to flag outdated.
descriptions./properties/fetched_at: UTC read timestamp (RFC 3339); the feed is a snapshot, not a live view.
descriptions./properties/truncated: True when a thread read failed, a host thread arrived with more comments than its cap returned, or a page walk stopped at the provider cap. The threads present are still trustworthy; the list may under-cover.
descriptions./properties/threads: One normalized thread per host root, in host order. A thread with a diff anchor is a review-comment; otherwise it is a conversation comment. Replies ride in comments[].
descriptions./$defs/thread: One review thread or conversation comment: host thread identity (what a resolution call takes), diff anchor and state, root author, and the replies.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/id: Host thread identity (GitHub reviewThreads id, GitLab discussion id, Bitbucket root comment id, Azure thread id, Forgejo comment id, GitCafe thread id). Empty when the payload carried none.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/path: Diff-relative path for a review-comment, empty for a conversation comment.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/line: End line of the anchor (the commented line for a single-line anchor), null when absent.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/start_line: First line of a multi-line anchor, null for a single-line anchor or a host with no range field.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/side: LEFT for a deleted-side anchor, RIGHT for an added/context anchor, null for a conversation comment or a host with no side.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/resolved: Host resolution state read from the host's own field: GitHub isResolved, GitLab note resolved, Azure thread status, Forgejo review-comment resolver, Bitbucket comment resolution, GitCafe resolved/resolvedAt. Hosts without a resolution field read false.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/outdated: True when the host says the anchor no longer maps to the current head: GitHub isOutdated, Bitbucket inline.outdated, GitLab position.head_sha differs from the feed head, Forgejo position 0 against a non-zero original_position, GitCafe outdated, Azure context without a line.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/url: Host-comment permalink when the payload carries one cheaply (GitHub url, Forgejo html_url, Bitbucket links.html.href); null otherwise.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/author: Root comment author handle or display name, empty when absent.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/author_kind: verdict when the root comment's final line is verdict's own hidden marker, bot when the host marks the author as a bot (or the login carries GitHub's [bot] suffix), else human.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/finding_sig: Finding signature linked from the root comment's hidden final-line verdict marker; null for threads verdict did not author and for summaries.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/kind: review-comment for a diff-anchored thread, issue-comment for a conversation comment.
descriptions./$defs/thread/properties/comments: Root comment first, then replies in host order. Each comment id is the id a reply call takes (GitHub databaseId).
descriptions./$defs/comment: One comment inside a thread: author identity/kind, the body excerpt, and the truncation flag.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/id: Host comment id (GitHub databaseId when present), empty when absent.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/author: Author handle or display name, empty when absent.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/author_kind: verdict when the comment's final line is verdict's own hidden marker, bot when the host marks the author as a bot (or the login carries GitHub's [bot] suffix), else human.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/body: Comment body, capped at 8 KiB; the raw provider file keeps the full text.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/truncated: True when body is an excerpt of a longer comment.
descriptions./$defs/comment/properties/created_at: Host creation timestamp (RFC 3339 when the host publishes one), empty when absent.

descriptions: The receipt `threads resolve` writes beside threads.json: the host, head, and timestamp of the mutation, the ids it closed, and the candidates it skipped with a machine-readable reason. A real run writes one host resolve call per id in resolved[]; a dry run writes no receipt and carries the plan in the envelope only. GitHub and GitLab carry the mutation; a host without a resolve endpoint refuses before this document is written.
descriptions./properties/schema_version: Receipt format version; only "1" is read.
descriptions./properties/provider: The host whose resolve call closed the threads.
descriptions./properties/pr: Pull request number the receipt belongs to.
descriptions./properties/head_sha: The head the thread feed was read at when the run selected its candidates.
descriptions./properties/dry_run: True only on a dry run; a real receipt is always false.
descriptions./properties/resolved: Host thread ids the run closed, in selection order.
descriptions./properties/skipped: Candidates the run left open, each with the reason it was skipped.
descriptions./$defs/skip: One skipped candidate: the host thread id and the machine-readable reason (already-resolved, no-finding-link, finding-not-addressed).
descriptions./$defs/skip/properties/id: Host thread id the selection considered.
descriptions./$defs/skip/properties/reason: Why the thread stayed open: already-resolved, no-finding-link (no finding marker), or finding-not-addressed (the local store does not mark the linked finding addressed).

descriptions: What the agent or a usage adapter hands the budget gate through VERDICT_USAGE: one measured run per record (a single object) or a run log (an array). The gate joins each record against past cost records by its window and prices comparable runs from usd, preferring it over the self-reported est_usd; records without usd never become a measured claim. verdict never discovers these files — the operator names them explicitly. Unknown keys are ignored, so newer writers stay readable.
descriptions./$defs/record/properties/source: Free-form measurer name (e.g. claude-code, opencode); carried into data.estimate.harness when the record prices a run.
descriptions./$defs/record/properties/model: Model that burned the tokens, when known; absent reads unknown, never priced.
descriptions./$defs/record/properties/tokens: Token counts for the window, when known; absent reads as unknown, never zero.
descriptions./$defs/record/properties/usd: Measured session price in USD, when the measurer priced it; the tool never prices tokens itself.
descriptions./$defs/record/properties/started_at: Window start (RFC 3339); the joined cost record's mtime must fall inside it.
descriptions./$defs/record/properties/ended_at: Window end (RFC 3339), never before the start.
descriptions./$defs/usageTokens: Token counts for one usage record: input and output plus the provider-reported cache subsets.
descriptions./$defs/usageTokens/properties/cache_read: Input tokens served from cache; a subset of input, never an addition.
descriptions./$defs/usageTokens/properties/cache_writ: Input tokens spent writing the cache; a subset of input, never an addition.

descriptions: The bundle's resolved review controls: fetch snapshots every control file at the PR base commit, and post/record refuse to trust the snapshot when its base or any used-file hash drifted. policy 'base' is the default; 'head' is the explicit --allow-head-controls opt-out.
descriptions./properties/schema_version: Snapshot format version; only "1" is trusted.
descriptions./properties/policy: base is the default base-owned rule set; head is the recorded opt-out.
descriptions./properties/base_sha: The bundle's base commit, the value post/record verify against.
descriptions./properties/sha: The commit the controls were read at; "" for the worktree opt-out.
descriptions./properties/files: One entry per inventory path, in inventory order.
descriptions./$defs/file: One control path's snapshot status: used entries carry the exact written bytes and SHA-256.
descriptions./$defs/file/properties/path: The inventory path, relative to the repository root (.verdict/...).
descriptions./$defs/file/properties/status: used means materialized and safe to read; missing means absent at the source.
descriptions./$defs/file/properties/bytes: The exact bytes written to the snapshot.
descriptions./$defs/file/properties/sha256: SHA-256 of the exact written bytes; post/record re-hash and refuse controls-stale on drift.
descriptions./properties/strict_input: When true, record promotes review.json warnings to errors and refuses while any remain. fetch resolves it from REVIEW_STRICT_INPUT=1 only; absent means off.

descriptions: One stored per-tree index under .verdict/index/trees/<tree>.json. Files are sorted by path, declarations and references stay in source order, and no timestamp or commit id lands here, so the same tree always writes the same bytes.
descriptions./$defs/file: One indexed file: its blob, package, imports, declarations, and references. An oversized or unparsable file carries the marker instead of silently disappearing from the coverage count.
descriptions./$defs/import: One import binding: the import path and the name it is bound to in the file.
descriptions./$defs/decl: One package-level declaration: name, kind, line, exported bit, and receiver type for a method.
descriptions./$defs/ref: One identifier reference: name, kind, qualifier for a package selector, source position, and whether it needs type information to resolve.

descriptions: The backtest score report, written to .verdict/backtest/<run>/report.json and echoed as the score envelope's data object: the same object, so one schema covers both. It grades each replayed PR's recorded findings against the bug lines the run's own SZZ candidate records, through the corpus matcher (+/-1 line, one finding per bug, text that names the defect kind). catch_rate is a match rate over blame-derived candidates, not a measured catch rate: a line a later fix deleted is a hypothesis about where a defect was, a deleted cleanup line beside the real bug is a candidate that was never defective, and an unmatched finding is not proven false.
descriptions./properties/prs: Replayed PRs whose recorded review was graded: the denominator of off_target_per_pr.
descriptions./properties/not_replayed: Mined candidates the run never scored (no resume row, or a row that recorded no review). Their bugs stay out of the denominators.
descriptions./properties/bugs: Ground-truth bug lines over the graded PRs: the denominator of catch_rate.
descriptions./properties/catch_rate: matched / bugs, rounded to four decimals; null when no PR was graded.
descriptions./properties/off_target_per_pr: (reported - matched) / prs, rounded to four decimals; null when no PR was graded. An unmatched finding is off target, never proven false.
descriptions./properties/unclassified: Graded bugs whose kind matched no rule, so no finding can name the defect and their lines can only lower catch_rate.
descriptions./properties/cost_per_review_usd: Priced spend over the priced reviews; null when no review reported a price. The mean of the priced reviews only.
descriptions./properties/spend: The priced spend: usd is the sum of the reported prices, null when none was priced, and a lower bound whenever unpriced_reviews is non-zero.
descriptions./properties/signals: One row per seed signal, fix first: the bugs a fix or a revert produced and how many a review named.
descriptions./$defs/spend/properties/usd: Sum of the prices the graded reviews reported; null when none was priced, never zero.
descriptions./$defs/spend/properties/priced_reviews: Graded reviews that reported a price.
descriptions./$defs/spend/properties/unpriced_reviews: Graded reviews that reported none; non-zero makes usd a lower bound.
descriptions./$defs/signal: One seed-signal row: bugs a fix or a revert introduced, and the matched count.

descriptions: Saved live calibration audit. Unknown outcomes are excluded from judged; resolution_rate is null without a judged denominator.
